stem:
The grouped frequency distribution of the weights (in kg) of 60 students is as follows.

Class: 40-50, Frequency: 8
Class: 50-60, Frequency: 14
Class: 60-70, Frequency: 20
Class: 70-80, Frequency: 12
Class: 80-90, Frequency: 6

The median class of the distribution is:

per_option_rationale.rationale: N/2 = 30. Cumulative frequencies: 8, 22, 42, 54, 60. The 30th value falls in the class 60-70 (CF before = 22, CF up to = 42). So median class is 60-70.
The student picks [50-60] because its cumulative frequency (22) is the highest CF still below N/2 = 30, confusing the class just before the median class with the median class itself.
Locating N/2 incorrectly at 36 (3N/5) and landing in class 70-80 instead of correctly using 30.
Choosing the first class, confusing the median class with the smallest observed class.

explanation: Median class is the class containing the (N/2)th value. N = 60, N/2 = 30. Build cumulative frequencies: 8, 22, 42. CF before class 60-70 is 22 and CF up to 60-70 is 42. Since 22 < 30 <= 42, the median class is 60-70.

explanation_sections.punchline: Median class = class where cumulative frequency first meets or exceeds N/2 = 30, which is 60-70.
explanation_sections.approach: Identify the model: median class in grouped data. Recipe: (1) compute N/2 = 60/2 = 30; (2) build cumulative frequency column: 8, 22, 42, 54, 60; (3) find first class where CF >= 30. CF of 40-50 = 8 (no), CF of 50-60 = 22 (no), CF of 60-70 = 42 (yes). Median class = 60-70.
explanation_sections.lesson: Always compute N/2 first, then identify the class in which cumulative frequency first reaches that value - not the class containing the mode or the highest frequency.
explanation_sections.timing: 35 seconds. Build cumulative column quickly (8, +14=22, +20=42). Check: 22 < 30 <= 42 so median class is 60-70. Trap: class 50-60 has CF 22 which is less than 30.
